Create a single independent full-resolution landscape 3:2 historical illustration for Pliny the Elder, Naturalis Historia, Book VI chapter 15, “Media and the Caspian Gates.” Ground it in the chapter’s transmitted ancient itinerary beyond the gates while treating that route geography as historical testimony, not settled modern fact. Abandon the usual sunset panorama and compose a cool blue-hour, water-level view from inside the pleasant oasis of Choara. The lower half is a broad dark irrigation basin with an unbroken mirror reflection. On a complete isolated rock rising beyond the water, show the entire compact stone city of Issatis from foundations to highest roof, wholly surrounded by sky and oasis foliage. Off to the left across the basin, place the complete low-walled city of Calliope among dense irrigated orchards. A narrow opening between the cities looks far across the pale Parthian desert toward the very small complete silhouette of Hecatompylos and a dim Caspian waterline. Emphasize the chapter’s contrast between enclosed desert and unexpectedly fertile Choara: four complete pomegranate and fig trees stand separately around the water, their trunks, roots, canopies, and reflections fully legible, with a slim gravity-fed channel entering the pool over carefully set ancient stones. No people, animals, caravan, gate, fortress, chariot, bridge, map, or route line. Use a deep inverted value structure unlike a daylight map view: luminous faded-lapis and muted-verdigris shadows dominate water and sky, pale ochre desert glows only through the central opening, and small madder fruit accents lead the eye toward the rock city. Keep the complete rock and city, low city, distant silhouette, all four trees, their reflections, basin edges, channel, waterline, and horizon fully inside generous uninterrupted image margins. One coherent continuous landscape, not an atlas, plan, or labelled reconstruction.

House style: an original deluxe Plinian natural-history folio rendered directly across a warm fibrous aged-vellum field, ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough and polished at once; precise iron-gall linework, fine cross-hatching and stipple; restrained translucent mineral pigments of umber, lampblack, muted verdigris, faded lapis, madder, and ochre. Historical-scene credibility without photography or glossy digital rendering. Maintain material continuity with a Roman natural-history codex, while giving this chapter a quiet nocturne-oasis dialect with strong reflections and intimate depth.

Absolutely no lettering, captions, labels, numerals, maps, arrows, route markings, legends, inscriptions, pseudo-writing, signatures, logos, watermarks, modern borders or nation claims, modern objects, panels, collage, decorative border, visible page edge, or repeated frames. No clipped tree, architecture, rock, reflection, water, or horizon. Output one complete opaque sRGB PNG at 1536×1024.
